title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 42
paragraphs: I wonder at those who have divided the world into Libya, Asia, and Europe, since the difference between these is not small; for in length Europe extends alongside both, while in breadth it is clearly, to my mind, beyond all comparison larger. Libya furnishes proofs about itself that it is surrounded by sea, except where it borders on Asia; and this fact was first shown by Necos the king of the Egyptians, of all those of whom we have knowledge. When he had ceased digging the channel leading from the Nile to the Arabian gulf, he sent Phoenicians with ships, bidding them sail and return through the Pillars of Heracles into the northern sea, and so back to Egypt. The Phoenicians, accordingly, set out from the Erythraian Sea and sailed through the southern sea. Whenever autumn came on, they would put in to shore and sow the land, wherever in Libya they happened to be as they sailed, and then they waited for the harvest. Having reaped the grain, they sailed on; so that after two years had passed, in the third year they turned through the Pillars of Heracles and arrived again in Egypt. They reported a thing I cannot believe, though another man may: namely, that in sailing round Libya they had the sun on their right hand.
